title: Validator and Repair Effects Under Shared-Initial-Candidate Semantics: A Paired Study of a Guarded LLM→NetOps Pipeline
abstract: We report a preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment measuring the effect of a deterministic validator and a bounded single-repair step applied to the same sampled LLM candidate (shared_initial_candidate semantics) in a guarded NetOps pipeline. The preregistered design targeted RAG-poisoning attacks, but the executed adapter contract disabled retrievals (retrieval_augmented_generation = false). Under the executed semantics the comparison is baseline single-shot validator outcome on a shared sampled candidate versus final guarded outcome (validator ± permitted repair) on that same candidate. On N = 250 synthetic intent→configuration tasks the deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) judged every sampled initial candidate valid (n11 = 250, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0), no repairs were applied, and baseline and guarded VALID_CONFIGURATION rates were identical (1.0). Actionable-misconfiguration = 1 − VALID_CONFIGURATION therefore equals 0 for both arms; paired difference = 0.0 (exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.0], 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Because retrieval augmentation was disabled in the executed contract, the preregistered RAG/poisoning hypotheses were not testable; we reconcile preregistration and execution artifacts, quantify the power/assumption mismatch, and give artifact-grounded recommendations for follow-up preregistered runs that exercise the original estimand.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to automate NetOps tasks such as intent→configuration translation, staged maintenance workflows, and zero‑touch configuration. Unconstrained generations can violate operational invariants (ordering, reachability, policy), so tool‑augmented pipelines that pair generation with deterministic validators and bounded repairs (generate→validate→repair) have been proposed as defensive architectures. Surveys and application papers document both the adoption of LLM-driven NetOps and continuing concerns about hallucination and constraint violations in operational artifacts [1]–[4].

We preregistered study candidate-2026-003-prereg-v1 to quantify whether targeted poisoning of retrieval contexts (RAG) increases actionable-misconfiguration rates and whether deterministic defenses mitigate that effect. The published preregistration defined a paired confirmatory design (N = 250 tasks), a primary poison fraction of 0.30, and a single primary estimand: the paired difference in actionable-misconfiguration rate (guarded minus baseline) under shared task instances. The executed adapter contract, however, used generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate and retrieval_augmented_generation = false (artifact-backed). Under these executed semantics the realized estimand differs from the conceptual RAG estimand: baseline and guarded begin from the same single sampled candidate and any paired difference can only arise from validator‑triggered repair. The present manuscript reports the artifact‑backed realized experiment, reconciles preregistration and execution, and draws evidence‑grounded recommendations for follow‑up preregistered runs.
sections.related_work:
Recent surveys and domain papers document LLM applications for NetOps and recommend tool augmentation to mitigate factual and constraint violations [1]–[4]. Benchmarks and framework papers (e.g., NetConfEval, NetLLMBench) provide task banks and evaluation primitives but highlight construct‑validity concerns for operational invariants such as reachability and policy compliance [5].

Adjacently, work on RAG pipelines and adversarial poisoning in security and code‑translation contexts reports concrete failure modes—hallucination, adversarial misinformation, and translation bugs—that motivate controlled adversarial evaluations for NetOps RAG pipelines [6]. Tool‑augmented proposals (LLMs calling deterministic verifiers or simulators) show promise for grounding generation but introduce latency and system‑design tradeoffs that complicate large‑scale deployment choices [7], [8]. The supplied literature set contains proposals and controlled demonstrations but lacks a broad topology‑grounded empirical measurement of RAG‑poisoning effects on operational invariants; that gap motivated our preregistration.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and primary estimand. The study was preregistered as candidate-2026-003-prereg-v1. The preregistration artifact is archived (preregistration SHA‑256: ebfbe67f56b5cfb4f0cdbf5a207c7cc095679771ab99515fa8d7d47b2f5e51e3) and defined H1: poisoning at poison_fraction = 0.30 increases actionable‑misconfiguration, and H2: deterministic retrieval filters reduce but do not eliminate poisoning effects. The preregistration specified a paired confirmatory design with N_confirmatory = 250 tasks and a complete_pair_primary exclusion rule. Power calibration assumed a baseline actionable‑misconfig ≈ 0.05 to detect an absolute paired increase ≈ 0.045–0.06 at 80% power.

Executed adapter contract and concrete runtime fields (artifact-backed). The run executed under adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1 with declared_model_version gpt-5-mini; see execution/model_configuration.json (sha256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Critical executed contract fields (archived) include: generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, retrieval_augmented_generation = false, initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1, maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1, task_count = 250, planned_episode_count = 500, completed_episode_count = 500, and model_calls_used = 250. The model configuration artifact records temperature = null (unset); null/unset must not be interpreted as temperature = 0 and is not evidence of deterministic hosted‑model sampling. These artifact facts are central to interpreting the realized estimand.

Shared‑initial‑candidate semantics and estimand meaning. Under the executed generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate exactly one sampled candidate was produced per task (shared_initial_generation stage) and that exact text was evaluated under both baseline and guarded conditions. Baseline is the deterministic validator's judgment on the shared sampled candidate. Guarded is the final outcome after the deterministic validator and at‑most‑one permitted repair applied only if the validator indicated a violation. Because baseline and guarded begin from the identical sampled candidate, differences can only come from the validator‑triggered repair step. We therefore treat the trial as a paired single‑candidate comparison: baseline single‑shot validator outcome versus final guarded outcome after deterministic validation/repair.

Validators, task bank, and scoring. The task bank comprised 250 deterministic synthetic intent→configuration tasks generated by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; representative entries and reference answers are archived under execution/task_manifest.jsonl (example reference answer sha256: c8b7cf48dce481e48bcd31621870c6b120d36b8f3879c74ce5a3a0142159d2c1). The validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5 issued per‑episode VALID_CONFIGURATION judgments and produced detailed validator_traces archived under execution/scoring/*.json (representative artifact hashes recorded in the manifest). The scoring rule used in confirmatory analysis was full_intent_constraint_validation, and actionable_misconfig was defined as 1 − VALID_CONFIGURATION.

Preregistered analysis plan and handling of missingness. The primary test was an exact McNemar two‑sided test for paired binary outcomes (α = 0.05) with paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI via 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). The registered analysis executor paired_binary_analysis_v1 implements this test. The preregistered missingness rule complete_pair_primary excludes any pair with missing condition outputs; the run produced zero exclusions. All analysis scripts and seeds are archived under analysis/ with hashes referenced in the execution manifest.

Deviations from preregistration (artifact‑grounded). The preregistration conceptualized a RAG‑poisoning experiment; the executed adapter contract—archived in execution/model_configuration.json (sha256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820) and summarized in execution/execution_manifest.json—explicitly set retrieval_augmented_generation = false. Because retrievals were disabled, the preregistered RAG/poisoning hypotheses were not testable in this run. The archived analysis_results metadata contains deviations_from_preregistration = [] while the executed contract contains the retrieval_flag noted above; we did not modify archived artifacts. To make the execution‑time realization machine‑visible in the manuscript we reference the two concrete artifacts above and document the executed semantics and their implications in this Methods section. See also execution/raw_results.jsonl (sha256: e3af400a9167c27f2255003a02cf86f7b75381f96c64697014b55b77e753514b) and deterministic_reconciliation.json (sha256: 92593e588656a3a4d1efd5492a3151f9d91bdafacc89c1a64c78b2535d27aa4f) for provider and stage accounting.
sections.results:
Execution accounting (artifact‑backed). The run started 2026-08-31T21:04:12Z and completed 2026-08-31T21:49:56Z (execution manifest). Planned episodes 500 (two conditions × 250 tasks) completed; failed_episode_count = 0. Provider‑call audit shows hosted_model_call_event_count = 250, cache_miss_count = 250, and one shared_initial_generation stage executed 250 times (no independent per‑condition sampling). Relevant artifact hashes: execution/model_configuration.json (sha256: a40e96e2...), execution/raw_results.jsonl (sha256: e3af400a9...), and execution/task_manifest.jsonl (sha256: da708045d3032bd6...).

Primary confirmatory outcomes (artifact‑backed). The paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; sha256: 1be58d8255423172b413b0f4908ac22bbf6527870fca0fd3dfa0d5908c987058) records n11 = 250, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Baseline VALID_CONFIGURATION rate = 250/250 = 1.0; guarded VALID_CONFIGURATION rate = 250/250 = 1.0. Consequently actionable_misconfig = 0 for every episode and the paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap 95% CI for the paired difference = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729). Analysis artifacts and logs are archived under analysis/ with hashes (analysis_log.jsonl sha256: f36cac00be2e6576...).

Representative artifacts and repair traces. Representative episode artifacts (e.g., execution/scoring/task-000004-baseline.json and task-000004-guarded.json; raw response sha256: 2d39d60d...) show identical shared_initial_candidate content across baseline and guarded arms, validator traces with validation_after.valid = true, and repair_applied = false. No repair_provider_trace entries exist because the guard never invoked repairs.

Power and assumption mismatch. The preregistered power calculation assumed baseline actionable_misconfig ≈ 0.05; the observed baseline = 0.0 violates that assumption. This mismatch reduces sensitivity to the originally targeted effect sizes and means the run cannot adjudicate the preregistered RAG poisoning hypotheses. The relevant analysis artifacts supporting these statements are analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (sha256: 1be58d82...) and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (sha256: f36cac00...).

Accounting and determinism checks. Deterministic_reconciliation.json (analysis artifact; sha256: 92593e58...) records complete_pair_count = 250, baseline_success_count = 250, guarded_success_count = 250, n_11 = 250, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0, and provider_call_audit: hosted_model_call_event_count = 250. model_configuration.json records temperature = null (unset); again, null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling of a hosted model and should not be interpreted as temperature = 0. The reconciliation artifact confirms that the run adhered to shared_initial_candidate semantics and the adapter's call budgeting.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation limited to the executed estimand. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics and the deterministic validator used, every sampled candidate satisfied validator checks for this synthetic task bank; therefore the guarded pipeline (validator ± allowed repair) could not alter paired outcomes and the paired difference is zero. This is an artifact‑grounded null effect of the validator/repair under the specific execution semantics and dataset.

What these results do not establish. The experiment did not exercise retrieval‑augmented generation (retrieval_augmented_generation = false), did not permit independent per‑condition sampling, used a single declared LLM (gpt-5-mini) and a single deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) on synthetic tasks; hence it cannot adjudicate the preregistered RAG‑poisoning hypotheses nor generalize to production deployments, vendor‑specific device behavior, or sampling variance across multiple model calls.

Threats to validity (artifact‑grounded). Internal validity: archived provider and reconciliation artifacts (deterministic_reconciliation.json; sha256: 92593e58...) confirm shared_initial_candidate semantics and one shared generation per task, isolating validator/repair effects but precluding detection of effects that require per‑condition sampling variability. Construct validity: the deterministic validator enforces a particular rule set (validator traces archived under execution/scoring/*.json) and may not capture vendor‑specific or asynchronous device behaviors that matter in production. External validity: synthetic task bank, single model, and single validator limit transferability to heterogeneous production topologies and multi‑model ensembles. Conclusion validity: the observed all‑success outcome yields exact CI bounds that reflect the controlled corpus rather than operational heterogeneity; preregistered power assumptions were violated and sensitivity to the original poisoning effect is therefore lacking.

Operational implications and concrete follow‑up preregistration steps. To test RAG‑poisoning and mitigation claims artifact‑groundedly we recommend a follow‑up preregistration that (a) enables retrieval_augmented_generation and deterministic poison injection at controlled poison_fraction levels, (b) permits independent per‑condition generation (generation_semantics ≠ shared_initial_candidate), (c) constructs a provenance‑flagged synthetic‑poison corpus with containment checks (see contamination_summary artifact placeholder), (d) broadens validators to vendor‑aware simulators, and (e) optionally evaluates multiple model sampling regimes and temperatures. Each of these steps corresponds to specific artifact changes relative to the present run (e.g., execution/model_configuration.json field toggles, additional provider call stages, and contamination_summary.csv entries) and should be preregistered with explicit seeds and containment rules as in the original plan.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment of a guarded generate→validate→repair NetOps pipeline under shared_initial_candidate semantics (declared model: gpt-5-mini; deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5; retrieval disabled). All 250 shared sampled candidates passed deterministic validation (n11 = 250), no repairs were applied, and the paired difference in actionable‑misconfiguration rate is 0.0 (exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.0]). Because retrieval augmentation was disabled in the executed contract, the preregistered RAG/poisoning hypotheses were not testable; we reconciled preregistration and execution artifacts and documented the executed semantics with concrete artifact references (execution/model_configuration.json sha256: a40e96e212ab87da..., preregistration sha256: ebfbe67f56b5...). Follow‑up preregistered runs that enable controlled retrieval augmentation, independent per‑condition sampling, broader validators, and multi‑model ensembles are necessary to measure guarded pipelines' mitigation potential under adversarial retrievals and sampling variability.

The archived model_configuration.json records temperature = null (unset); null/unset is not evidence of deterministic hosted-model sampling and must not be interpreted as temperature = 0. All raw outputs, validator traces, analysis scripts, paired contingency artifacts, and the full execution manifest are archived and referenced by the submission (see execution/raw_results.jsonl sha256: e3af400a9167c27f2255003a02cf86f7b75381f96c64697014b55b77e753514b and analysis artifacts with hashes in the execution manifest).
limitations: The executed design used generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate with exactly one sampled initial generation per task reused across arms; it therefore measures validator/repair effects on the same candidate and cannot detect differences that require independent per-condition generation variability.

Retrieval-augmented generation was disabled in the executed adapter (retrieval_augmented_generation = false); the preregistered poisoning/RAG hypotheses and dose–response analyses were therefore not testable in this run and are recorded as an execution-time realization documented in execution/model_configuration.json (sha256: a40e96e2...) and the execution manifest.

Observed VALID_CONFIGURATION = 1 for all episodes yields no repair events; absence of repair activity in this run does not demonstrate that repairs cannot be useful under different sampling, retrieval, or adversarial conditions.

A single declared LLM (gpt-5-mini) and a single deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) were used on synthetic tasks; these choices limit external validity to diverse production topologies, vendor semantics, and multi-model ensembles.

The model configuration recorded temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling—hosted-model nondeterminism may remain and is logged in archived provider traces. The observed zero-event outcome (no actionable misconfigs) violates the preregistered baseline-rate assumption (≈0.05) and therefore does not constitute a sensitive test of the original poisoning hypothesis.
